conceptual assets.information: The compressed instruction encoding and its corresponding 32-bit decoded instruction are the operation information used by the CPU for instruction execution. The encoding enters through instr_i and the decoded operation leaves through instr_o.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: An integrator may treat instruction code as proprietary, and the decoded instruction is exposed at instr_o through lines 299-301. Correct CPU execution depends on the input-dependent decoded fields, which can be altered to produce a different instruction through the assignments in lines 72-285 and the output assignments in lines 299-301.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe instr_o to recover proprietary instruction content or tamper with the instruction path so that the CPU executes a different decoded instruction.

conceptual assets.information: The legality decision records whether the input encoding is accepted as a legal compressed instruction and controls suppression of one output bit for illegal encodings. It has no independent entry or exit port because instr_i only decides it and illegal only decides instr_o.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The legality decision is an integrity-sensitive control result because corrupting illegal can cause an illegal encoding to be accepted or a legal instruction to be altered at instr_o; it is generated by the input-dependent checks and assignments at lines 61, 77-78, 98-100, 153-154, 180-181, 203-204, 221-222, 232-234, 245-246, 256-258, 266-267, 289-291 and controls line 300.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could fault-inject or otherwise alter the legality decision so an illegal encoding passes through or a legal instruction is corrupted at instr_o.
